technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the HDFS sink as a registered streaming module using the existing module lifecycle, message contract, configuration conventions, and Hadoop client APIs already supported by the target codebase.

Expose Hadoop shell commands through the existing shell command abstraction, with command parsing, validation, filesystem interaction, and user-readable error handling isolated from end-to-end deployment.

Use an expression-based binding mechanism compatible with the existing Spring messaging and configuration model so module properties can be resolved from incoming message headers, payloads, or other message metadata.

Move the JDBC and Kafka modules by preserving their externally visible configuration and message contracts wherever practical, while adapting package names, build metadata, module registration, and repository-specific integration points.

Represent composed jobs as versioned definitions stored through a repository abstraction, allowing the initial implementation to use a simple persistent backend while leaving room for alternative repository implementations.
Orchestrate composed jobs through a workflow service that validates definitions, resolves dependencies, submits or starts constituent jobs, and reports aggregate state and failures.
Use unit and focused integration tests for shell commands and module behavior, reserving full deployment tests for a smaller set of cross-component verification scenarios.
assumptions: The target repositories, build system, module registry, shell framework, job runtime, and test conventions already exist and can be extended without a platform rewrite.
The increment targets the existing Spring XD or Spring Cloud Data Flow-era APIs used by the user stories; a migration to a newer major platform is out of scope.
Hadoop client libraries and compatible test dependencies can be added through the existing dependency-management process, and a live Hadoop cluster is not required for most automated tests.

The HDFS sink needs standard write behavior, configurable destination and serialization options, and basic error handling, but advanced features such as transactions, exactly-once semantics, encryption, and high-availability tuning are out of scope.
Hadoop shell support is limited to the commonly required filesystem query and manipulation commands rather than implementing the complete Hadoop command-line tool.

The composed-job repository work includes selecting and implementing one viable repository option plus a repository abstraction; production support for multiple database or remote repository backends is out of scope.
Composed-job orchestration reuses the existing job deployment and monitoring mechanisms and does not introduce a new workflow engine.
Message binding supports the module properties needed by the current modules and common expression forms; arbitrary user-defined scripting and complex transformation expressions are out of scope.
The JDBC and Kafka moves are repository/module relocations with compatibility updates, not complete redesigns of either connector.

One developer performs analysis, implementation, testing, documentation, code review preparation, and integration work; estimates are person-workdays and exclude waiting time for external teams or infrastructure.

The estimates include normal defect correction discovered during development and focused validation, but not major architectural changes revealed by unavailable source code or undocumented compatibility requirements.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing module registry, shell framework, job lifecycle, message binding, repository abstractions, JDBC and Kafka modules, build configuration, and test infrastructure; produce an implementation plan and identify compatibility constraints.

Implement the HDFS sink, add Hadoop dependencies and configuration, integrate it with the module registry, implement message-to-file writing and error handling, and add unit and focused integration tests.
Add Hadoop filesystem command parsing, validation, execution, output formatting, and error handling to the shell while following existing command conventions and configuration behavior.
Create or extend shell command test fixtures and mocks, cover command parsing, successful execution, invalid input, filesystem failures, and output behavior without requiring full stream deployment.

Evaluate repository options against definition storage, lookup, update, versioning, and operational requirements; document the decision; implement the repository abstraction and the selected initial backend with tests.

Implement composed-job definition validation, constituent-job dependency handling, submission or startup sequencing, aggregate status tracking, failure handling, and operational commands or service endpoints, with workflow tests.

Design and implement binding of incoming message payloads, headers, and properties to module configuration through expressions or equivalent metadata resolution; update representative modules and add security, validation, and compatibility tests.

Move the JDBC module into the streaming-services repository, update packages, build metadata, registrations, configuration, documentation, and tests, and verify sink behavior and compatibility with existing pipelines.

Move the Kafka module into the streaming-services repository, update packages, build metadata, registrations, configuration, documentation, and tests, and verify source behavior and compatibility with existing pipelines.

Integrate the new and migrated modules with shared build and release configuration, update usage documentation and examples, verify registry discovery and configuration metadata, and resolve cross-module compatibility issues.
Run the relevant unit, integration, and selected end-to-end tests; diagnose and fix increment-related defects; perform cleanup, release-note updates, and prepare the complete change set for delivery.
